counterparty.name: Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL)

items.expectedFix: Replace the cap with at least a mutual 12-month-fees cap and make indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct uncapped; preferably use the greater of 12 months' paid-or-payable fees and USD 1,000,000 and add the other preferred carve-outs.
items.note: The main Agreement mutually excludes consequential damages and caps both parties at 3% of the bill-of-materials value for Products delivered from the Effective Date through claim resolution. The cap lacks the required carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct and may be materially below 12 months' fees. The separate contractual limitations period does not cure these defects.

items.expectedFix: No customer-side change is required.
items.note: The separate Equipment and Program Loan Agreement caps and excludes only IBM's liability. Because IBM is Customer, this is customer-favourable and does not cap MSL's liability under that agreement. The action limitation is not itself a liability cap.

items.expectedFix: Carve MSL's indemnification obligations out of the general cap or apply a super-cap of at least three times annual fees.
items.note: MSL provides IBM a substantive IP, legal-compliance and warranty indemnity with customary notice, cooperation, defence control and infringement remedies. However, the indemnity is not carved out of the unusually low 3% general liability cap and therefore does not reach the fallback super-cap protection.

items.expectedFix: No change is required.
items.note: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds IBM. Any product-use limitations instead bind MSL.

items.expectedFix: No change is required.
items.note: No sole-supplier or exclusive-purchasing obligation binds IBM.

items.expectedFix: No customer-side change is required.
items.note: The redacted favourable-treatment provisions and the express most-favoured-customer tooling term require MSL to extend favourable pricing or treatment to IBM. They benefit, rather than burden, Customer.

items.expectedFix: Delete the restriction or make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the services for no more than 12 months after their involvement, and retain the existing general-advertising and unsolicited-approach exceptions.
items.note: IBM is prohibited from soliciting all Transferred Employees for a redacted number of years. Although unsolicited approaches and general advertising are carved out, the restriction is one-way, begins at the Effective Date rather than the employee's involvement, and its redacted duration cannot be confirmed as 12 months.

items.expectedFix: Add an IBM right to terminate the Outsourcing Agreement for convenience on 30 days' notice, with no fee and a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; fallback notice may not exceed 90 days and any fee must be capped at three months' fees.
items.note: The three-year Outsourcing Agreement permits termination for cause but gives IBM no general right to terminate for convenience. The convenience right in the separate confidentiality agreement does not terminate the outsourcing commitment.

items.expectedFix: Confirm a notice period acceptable under the playbook and separately add IBM's convenience-termination right to the Outsourcing Agreement.
items.note: The incorporated confidentiality agreement is terminable for convenience by either party, but the notice period is redacted and the right applies only to that ancillary agreement. It therefore cannot be confirmed against the notice standard and does not cure the missing right under the Outsourcing Agreement.

items.expectedFix: Require mutual written renewal or reduce IBM's non-renewal notice deadline to no more than 60 days, preferably 30 days with a 60-day reminder.
items.note: The three-year Agreement automatically renews for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives six months' notice. The approximately 180-day non-renewal window exceeds the 90-day walkaway threshold.

items.expectedFix: Make renewal mutual or permit IBM to opt out on no more than 60 days' notice.
items.note: The Statement of Work automatically renews for six-month periods but requires 12 months' advance notice. This exceeds the walkaway threshold and effectively requires notice before the renewal period begins.

items.expectedFix: No required change; optionally specify exclusive state and federal courts in New York County.
items.note: The main Agreement applies New York law and requires actions to be brought in a court located in New York State. This uses an accepted jurisdiction, although it does not specify New York County.

items.expectedFix: No required change; venue may optionally be aligned with the main Agreement.
items.note: The separate Equipment and Program Loan Agreement is governed by New York law and contains no adverse foreign forum or arbitration requirement.

items.expectedFix: Permit IBM to assign without consent to affiliates and successors in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. Require only notice for successor assignments, make consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld, and prohibit MSL assignment to an IBM competitor.
items.note: The main Agreement and confidentiality agreement prohibit IBM from assigning without MSL's consent and provide no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out. MSL receives a consent standard for certain affiliate assignments, while IBM does not. MSL's separate change-of-control notice and the EPLA restriction on MSL do not cure IBM's blanket restriction.

items.expectedFix: No required change; an express perpetual licence to any retained MSL background IP embedded in Products could be added for clarity.
items.note: MSL assigns IBM all intellectual and industrial property rights in delivered Products and related inventions. The direction benefits Customer and does not assign IBM IP or data to MSL.

items.expectedFix: No required change; clarify that any retained MSL background IP embedded in a Product is licensed perpetually, irrevocably and royalty-free to IBM and its affiliates, contractors and successors.
items.note: IBM receives ownership of the Product-related deliverables and inventions, which is broader than a customer-use licence. The agreement does not make IBM's rights revocable or exclude IBM affiliates and contractors from using Customer-owned deliverables.

items.expectedFix: Consolidate ordinary audits to once per 12 months on at least 15 days' notice, during business hours, through a confidential independent auditor, at IBM's cost unless a material discrepancy exceeds 10%. Preserve narrowly tailored additional audits only for reasonable suspected violations.
items.note: IBM receives several audit and inspection rights, including access at all reasonable times, regular monitoring, access as IBM deems necessary, and semiannual licence audits. Some regimes include business-hours limits, advance notice and an independent auditor, but the package is not limited to once annually and certain inspections require only 48 hours' notice.

items.expectedFix: No customer-side change is required.
items.note: The responsiveness penalty and Product Recall costs are payable by MSL to IBM. They benefit Customer and are not liquidated damages payable by IBM.

items.expectedFix: Specify at least a 90-day product/software warranty and 30-day services warranty, preferably 12 months and 90 days respectively, and add express compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties where software services apply.
items.note: MSL expressly warrants conformity, quality, workmanship and freedom from defects, with repair, replacement or refund remedies, and the disclaimer preserves those express warranties. The Parts, workmanship and acceptance periods are redacted, so compliance with the minimum duration cannot be confirmed.

items.expectedFix: Add MSL CGL coverage of USD 1M per occurrence/USD 2M aggregate, E&O of at least USD 1M, cyber/privacy coverage of at least USD 2M where data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request.
items.note: The agreement requires replacement-value coverage for consigned Products and states that IBM will insure IBM-owned tooling, with MSL jointly insured where possible. These CUAD-located provisions do not establish MSL commercial general liability, E&O or cyber coverage, so the required vendor insurance package appears substantively absent.

items.expectedFix: No change is required.
items.note: IBM may cancel purchase orders, and forecasts expressly do not obligate IBM to purchase Products. The CUAD span is a vendor defect-free production target, not a minimum purchase commitment on IBM.

items.expectedFix: Require up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, with at least 90 days guaranteed, return or export of all IBM data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion after successful return.
items.note: MSL must assist with transferring responsibilities and Products, return IBM documentation and software media, and complete certain inventory reconciliations. However, no minimum transition-assistance period, standard-format data export deadline or comprehensive deletion certification is provided; several CUAD spans concern records, asset purchases or immediate cessation rather than transition support.
